status: frozen before any measurement; verdict.ts reads this file; no threshold moves after the data

terms.unit: one (instrument, cell, load point). cell = (rtt, mix, shape, sharing); load point = closed-loop at the highest caller count, or open-loop at a fraction of the cell's saturation throughput
terms.config: control | fixed:D for each D in fixedGrid | rtt-aware | latency-aware | aimd
terms.candidates: control, fixed:<D*>, rtt-aware, latency-aware, aimd. The per-cell best fixed D is an oracle bound and never a candidate.

loadPoints.saturation: T* = largest median closed-loop throughput at closedForRule over every config in the same (instrument, cell); open-loop arrival rate = fraction x T* statements per second, Poisson arrivals, latency from the scheduled send time
loadPoints.openOverload: an open-loop run is overloaded when fast statements are still incomplete 3000 ms after the last scheduled arrival; the incomplete ones count with their age at that moment (right-censored). Overloaded runs stay in the rule: a policy that cannot carry the rate loses on p99.9.

fastP999.unit: ms, fast statements, from scheduled send time

slowP99.unit: ms, slow statements, defined when the mix has slow statements

cpuPerStatement.unit: microseconds of client CPU per completed statement (simulator: modelled from the fitted cost model)

noise.withinNoiseOfBest: candidate median is no worse than the best candidate's worst run, on every metric defined in the unit (best = best median per metric)

wins.definition: a policy wins somewhere when, in at least one valid unit, its worst run beats the best run of the simplest within-noise policy of that unit by margin or more on a metric

default: the simplest candidate that is within noise of the best in every required unit; if none exists the verdict names the unit and the margin

fixedDSelection.reference: best median per metric over every config of the unit, the whole fixed grid included
fixedDSelection.d_star: the fixed D that is within noise of that reference in the most required units; ties: lower geometric-mean regret (median / reference median, lower-better inverted), then smaller D

validity.indicative: fewer completed fast statements in any run of the unit: unit stays out of the rule
validity.clientBound: median client CPU utilisation (CPU seconds / wall seconds of the load generator process) at or above this value for any candidate config of the unit: unit stays out of the rule
validity.correctness: a result delivered to the wrong caller (unique id mismatch), a reordered result inside a pipeline, or one statement's error failing another puts that config out of that unit, whatever its speed

requiredUnits.simulator: units of the full simulated matrix; counted in the verdict only when the simulator passes validation (criterion below); otherwise labelled exploratory and excluded
requiredUnits.sharing: the rule is evaluated separately for sharing off and sharing on, and each is reported

simulatorValidation.calibrateOn: real loopback and one delayed (20 ms) fast-only cells
simulatorValidation.predictHeldOut: every other real cell (mixed loads, pipelines, the 4 ms point, PgBouncer)
simulatorValidation.criterion: simulated median throughput within 15% of the real median, and the same policy ranking in every real cell where policies differ beyond noise
simulatorValidation.onFailure: label the simulator exploratory and keep it out of the rule

simplicity: results/simplest.json, produced by scripts/simplest.ts before any measurement: fewer tunable constants, then fewer policy code lines, then the order of the brief
